sanskrit: ava mā pāpman sṛja vaśī san mṛḍayāsi naḥ | ā mā bhadreṣu dhāmasu tvaṃ dhehy avihrutam ||
english: Release me from evil, O sin, being subdued, grant us ease. Place me, unstraying, in auspicious abodes.

sanskrit: yo mā pāpman na jahāsi tam u tvā jahimo vayam | anyatrāsman ny ucya sahasrākṣāmartya ||
english: That evil which does not abandon me — we abandon it. Be spoken away from us elsewhere, O thousand-eyed immortal.

sanskrit: pathor vayaṃ vyāvartane niṣpāpmānaṃ suvāmasi | yo no dveṣṭi taṃ gaccha yaṃ dviṣmas taṃ jahi ||
english: At the turning of the road we press out one freed from sin. Go to him who hates us; strike down him whom we hate.

sanskrit: śava ivāsi saṃnaddho na bhogam avidaṃ tvayi | śiro bhinadmi te pāpman yathā na punar āyasi ||
english: You are bound up like a corpse; I have found no enjoyment in you. I split your head, O sin, so that you may not come again.

sanskrit: indro asmān divā pātu mṛtyoḥ pāśāt svastaye | dyaur no madhyataḥ pātu bhūmī rājñī svastaye ||
english: May Indra guard us by day from the snare of death, for well-being. May Heaven guard us in our midst, may Earth the queen guard us, for well-being.

sanskrit: sūryo asmān divā pātu mṛtyoḥ pāśāt svastaye | vāto no madhyataḥ pātv ahorātrī svastaye ||
english: May the Sun guard us by day from the snare of death, for well-being. May the Wind guard us in our midst; may Day-and-Night guard us, for well-being.

sanskrit: somo asmān divā pātu mṛtyoḥ pāśāt svastaye | āpo no madhyataḥ pāntu mā no nirṛtir īśata ||
english: May Soma guard us by day from the snare of death, for well-being. May the Waters guard us in our midst; may Dissolution not rule over us.

sanskrit: saṃ vāṃ cakṣuḥ saṃ hṛdayaṃ manasāvīvanaṃ manaḥ | asyāḥ sarūpavatsāyā ghṛte homena sarpiṣā ||
english: Together be your sight, together your heart, together your mind uniting with mind — through ghee, through the oblation with clarified butter, for this cow whose calf is of the same form.

sanskrit: yat kakṣīvān saṃvananaṃ putro aṅgirasām avet | tena vām adya devāḥ saṃ priyā sam avīvanan ||
english: The charm of union which Kakṣīvān, son of the Aṅgirasas, knew — with that charm the gods have today united you two beloved ones together.

sanskrit: saṃvananaṃ vāṃ manaso atho saṃvananaṃ hṛdaḥ | atho bhagasya yac chrāntaṃ tena saṃ vānayāmi vām ||
english: The union-charm of your minds, and the union-charm of your hearts — and what portion of Bhaga is exhausted — with that I unite you two.

sanskrit: ahaṃ te manasā manaś cakṣur gṛhṇāmi cakṣuṣā | evā pari ṣvajasva mā yathāsan mayi te manaḥ ||
english: I seize your mind with my mind, your eye with my eye. Embrace me thus, so that your mind may be fixed in me.

sanskrit: ā rathasyeva cakre abhi mā vartatām asau | reṣmacchinnaṃ yathā tṛṇaṃ veṣṭāsau manasā mayi ||
english: Let that one turn toward me as the two wheels of a chariot. Let that one wind around me in mind, like a blade of grass severed by a sickle.

sanskrit: pari tvā yātur asaraṃ pari mātuḥ pari svasuḥ | pari tvānyābhya strībhyo 'nayauṣadhyāsaram ||
english: I have gone around you with this herb — away from the sorceress, away from the mother, away from the sister; I have gone around you away from other women with this herb.

sanskrit: ya indrasya sabhādhāno yasmin samitim āsate | hiraṇyaṃ yasya parṇāni tasmā aśvattha te namaḥ ||
english: You who are the assembly-hall of Indra, in whom they sit at council, whose leaves are gold — to you, O Aśvattha tree, homage.

sanskrit: yaḥ śākhābhir antarikṣam ā pūrayati niṣṭhayā | chandāṃsi yasya parṇāni tasmā aśvattha te namaḥ ||
english: You who fill the atmosphere with branches, downward-rooted, whose leaves are the sacred metres — to you, O Aśvattha tree, homage.

sanskrit: yaṃ mṛgo na samāpnoti pakṣābhyāṃ śakuniṣ patan | divaṃ yaḥ sarvāṃ stabhnāti tasmā aśvattha te namaḥ ||
english: You whom the deer does not reach, nor the bird flying on its wings — you who prop up the entire sky — to you, O Aśvattha tree, homage.

sanskrit: jyeṣṭhaghnyāṃ jāto vicṛtor yamasya māyaṃ hiṃsīḥ pitarau vardhamānaḥ | syonau vyāghrā uta te śivau stām ati neṣaṃ duritāni viśvā ||
english: Born under the star Jyeṣṭhaghni, released from Yama's snare — growing up, may you not harm your parents. May your two tigers be gentle and auspicious; may all misfortunes pass over you.

sanskrit: vyāghre ahny ajaniṣṭa vīro nakṣatrajāḥ sarvavīraḥ suvīraḥ | sa mā hiṃsīḥ pitarau vardhamānas tasya te devāḥ prati gṛhṇantu homam ||
english: A hero was born on a tiger-day, born of the nakṣatra, full of heroes, well-heroic. Growing up, may he not harm his parents; may the gods accept the oblation for him.

sanskrit: yā rohiṇīr devapatyā pra dhenur iva pinvate | tatra tisro vyaṣṭakāḥ sarvām̐ adhi bruvantu prajāyai jagate ca vām ||
english: The Rohiṇī stars, wives of the gods, swell like a milk cow — there let the three Vyaṣṭakā festivals speak over all, for offspring and for the living world, for you both.

sanskrit: yad ārdrābhyām araṇibhyāṃ devāḥ śakrā amanthaṃ puruṣeṇa puruṣam | atrāpuṣyataṃ mithunā sayonī jīvāṃ prajāṃ jaradaṣṭiṃ sutejasā ||
english: When the powerful gods churned fire-drill with fire-drill, person with person in the damp wood — here let that pair of the same womb flourish, a living offspring reaching old age with splendid brilliance.

sanskrit: hataṃ pataṅgam uta tardam ākhum aśvinā bhintaṃ śiro mṛṇataṃ hanū dataḥ | yathā naḥ sasyaṃ na ghasaṃ vyadvarā evābhayaṃ kṛṇutaṃ dhānyāya naḥ ||
english: O Aśvins, smite the locust and the tarda-bird and the mouse; split the head, grind the jaws and teeth. So that they may not devour our grain and rend it — make for us freedom from fear for our grain.

sanskrit: tarda hai pataṅga hai jabhya hā upakvasa | anadanta idaṃ dhānyam ahiṃsanto apodita ||
english: Ho, tarda-bird! Ho, locust! Ho, jabhya and upakvasa! — not eating this grain, not harming it, be driven away!

sanskrit: tardapate vaghāpate tṛṣṭadaṃśmā śṛṇota naḥ | hotrevāprāśitaṃ havir vṛkṇajihvā upādhvam ||
english: O lord of tarda-birds, lord of the vagha, O sharp-toothed one — hear us. The oblation unsavored, like a hotr priest's offering, approach with clipped tongues!

sanskrit: tarda jabhyāpijihvayā ya imaṃ divyaṃ pīyūṣaṃ prathamas titṛpsāt | taṃ pratyañcam arciṣā vidhya marman ||
english: O tarda, with the jabhya's lapping tongue — whoever first seeks to satiate himself on this heavenly ambrosia — pierce him face-on at the vital spot with a flame.

sanskrit: ye abhrajā ye vātajā ye divas pari jajñire | marīcyāḥ putrāṇāṃ vayam api nahyāma āsyam ||
english: Those born from clouds, those born from the wind, those who came into being from the sky — we bind shut the mouths of the sons of Marīci.

sanskrit: ye arjunā ye haritā ye kṛṣṇā ye ca rohitāḥ | kabandhasya praśāsane śalabhyāñ jambhayāmasi ||
english: The white ones, the green ones, the black ones, and the red ones — under the command of Kabandha, we crush the locusts.

sanskrit: antarikṣeṇa patata mā sasyam abhi paddhvam | girīṇāṃ sānuṣu sīdata tṛṇaṃ kapālam attana śalabhās tad viśām iva ||
english: Fly through the atmosphere; do not fall upon the grain. Settle on the ridges of the mountains; eat grass and potsherds, O locusts — that is as your people.

sanskrit: yathāśvāso yathā dhuraṃ yuktā vahanti sādhuyā | evā mūtra pra bhidyasva vi vaster āsyaṃ sṛja ||
english: Just as horses harnessed to a yoke draw well — so, urine, burst forth; open and release the mouth of the bladder.

sanskrit: viṣitaṃ te vastibilaṃ samudrasyodadher iva | pra te bhinadmi mehanaṃ vartraṃ veśantyā iva ||
english: Opened is your bladder's hole, like the ocean's vessel. I split open your urinary passage — the obstruction — as if opening a dam.

sanskrit: yāḥ samudrād uccaranti jaratīr upajihvikāḥ | pramehaṇasya tā vidur ubhayor mehanasya ca ||
english: Those aged ones, the tongue-lickers, who rise from the ocean — they know the cure of urinary disease and of both urinary organs.

sanskrit: śīrṣṇo valīr āsno valīr aṅgādaṅgān mukhād valīḥ | sarvās tā indrāṇī valīr apa mārṣṭv adhi tvacaḥ ||
english: The wrinkles of the head, the wrinkles of the face, the wrinkles from limb to limb, from the mouth — may Indrāṇī wipe away all those wrinkles from the skin.

sanskrit: yās tvaci valayo jātā yā jātās tanvas pari | sarvās tā indrāṇī valīḥ śamīśākhāsv ā sajāt ||
english: The wrinkles that were born on the skin, those that came into being around the body — may Indrāṇī attach all those wrinkles onto the branches of the Śamī tree.

sanskrit: ā śamīṃ māmakī valī rurohāti jahāti mām | etām indrasya jāyā validhānīm akṛṇvata ||
english: My wrinkle has climbed up the Śamī tree and forsaken me. This one Indra's wife made the receptacle of wrinkles.

sanskrit: yathā sūryo nakṣatrāṇāṃ varcāṃsi yuvate divaḥ | evā sapatnānām ahaṃ varca indriyam ā dade ||
english: Just as the Sun draws to itself the brilliances of the nakṣatras in the sky — so I take to myself the splendor and vital force of my rivals.

sanskrit: yac ca varcaḥ sapatnānāṃ bhrātṛvyeṣu ca yad yaśaḥ | tad indro vṛtrahā dhātā savitā dīdharan mayi ||
english: Whatever brilliance belongs to my rivals, whatever fame resides among my adversaries — may Indra the slayer of Vṛtra, Dhātā, and Savitā make that shine within me.

sanskrit: yāś ca gāvaḥ sapatnānāṃ bhrātṛvyeṣu ca yad vasu | tan nir jyeyam iva jītvā savitā dīdharan mayi ||
english: Whatever cattle belong to my rivals, whatever wealth lies among my adversaries — having won it as if by conquest in a game, may Savitā make that shine within me.

sanskrit: satyam eva jayatu nānṛtaṃ satyasya panthā ṛjur astu sādhuḥ | satyaṃ vadantaḥ samidhe vidhema satyena dyāvāpṛthivī aprathetām ||
english: Truth alone shall conquer, not falsehood; the path of truth shall be straight and good. Speaking truth, let us tend the sacred fire; by truth did Heaven and Earth spread apart.

sanskrit: vāgbhāgasya ca satyena rudrasya sumanasyayā | indreṇādhibruvatā vayaṃ viśaṃ prāśi videmahi ||
english: By the truth of Vāgbhāga, by the benevolence of Rudra, and with Indra pronouncing over it — may we know dominion over the people and the power of speech.

sanskrit: yā te rudreṣur āyatā vāci vā te araṃkṛtā | yenedaṃ vivadāmahe tasya prāśaṃ tvaṃ jahi ||
english: That arrow of yours, O Rudra, which is aimed at speech, or that which is fitted to it — the means by which we quarrel — destroy the injury caused by that.

sanskrit: jahi tvaṃ tasya prāśam uta satyām utānṛtām | yo asmān indra vṛtrahan vācā prāśaṃ jigīṣati ||
english: Destroy the injury caused by that — whether the true or the false — by him who, O Indra slayer of Vṛtra, seeks to conquer us in speech through injury.

sanskrit: ut pramut prāṇa bahvīha sīdedaṃ pṛṇa | utodiva sma siñcatāt samudrasyeva madhyataḥ ||
english: Rise up, burst upward, O breath; settle here abundantly, fill this. And let it pour from above as if from the midst of the ocean.

sanskrit: samudraś ca śatadhāraḥ sahasradhāro akṣitaḥ | purastād indra ācarat pūrṇagoṣṭha idaṃ pṛṇa ||
english: The ocean with a hundred streams, with a thousand streams, inexhaustible — Indra moving from the east, O full cattle-pen, fill this.

sanskrit: ihopa pṛṇa saṃ pṛṇa vṛṣa prajananāḥ kṛdhi | iha gāvaḥ pra jāyadhvam ihāśvā iha pūruṣāḥ | iho sahasradakṣiṇo abhi prāśā ni ṣīdatu ||
english: Fill here, fill full here; O bull, make the procreative organs active. Here let cows be born, here horses, here men. Let the one with a thousand gifts of honor here settle upon the territory.

sanskrit: jyeṣṭhaghnyai nakṣatrāṇām ahne rātryā idaṃ namaḥ | juhomi viśvakarmaṇe sa śivo mṛḍayāti naḥ ||
english: To Jyeṣṭhaghni, to the nakṣatras, to day, to night — this homage. I offer to Viśvakarman; may he, being gracious, show us mercy.

sanskrit: mā jyeṣṭhaṃ vadhīd ayam agna eṣāṃ mūlabarhaṇaṃ pari vṛṇakty enam | grāhyāḥ pāśān vi cṛta prajānan pitāputrau mātaraṃ muñca sarvān ||
english: May this one not slay the firstborn, O Agni; he strips away the root-destroying one from them. Loosen the snares of the seizure, knowing it; free the father, the son, the mother — release them all.

sanskrit: un muñca pāśāṃs tvam agna eṣāṃ trayas tribhir utthitā yebhir āsan | māyaṃ hiṃsīḥ pitaraṃ vardhamāno mā mātaraṃ pra minīr yā janitrī ||
english: Release their snares, O Agni — the three that were raised up in threes, by which they were bound. Growing up, may this one not harm the father; may he not harm the mother who bore him.

sanskrit: grāhyāḥ pāśān vi cṛta ye sinanti yāṃ brahmaṇā parivṛñjanti vedhasaḥ | un muñca pāśāṃs tvam agna eṣāṃ tvajjātasyānv ahar-ahar astu bhadram ||
english: Loosen the snares of the seizure that bind — her whom the wise ones guard with sacred formulas. O Agni, release their bonds; day after day may well-being follow for the one born of you.

sanskrit: ni vartadhvaṃ mānu gāta- -asmān siṣakta revatīḥ | agnīṣomā punarvasū asya vardhayataṃ rayim ||
english: Turn back; do not go away — let the Revatī stars cling to us. O Agni and Soma, O Punarvasu, increase the wealth of this one.

sanskrit: punar enā ni vartaya punar enā upā kuru | indra enā ni yacchatv agnir enā upājatu ||
english: Turn these back again; bring these close again. Let Indra hold these back; let Agni come to them.

sanskrit: pari vo viśvato dadha ūrjā ghṛtena payasā | ye devāḥ ke ca yajñiyās te rayyā saṃ sṛjantu mā ||
english: I place around you on all sides strength, ghee, and milk. Whatever gods are worthy of sacrifice — may they unite me with riches.
